S13v6-1P4: Also in the meantime, budget what the group can provide on the practical side. Water, housing, food stores, health care. Tools, seasonal labor, transport, schooling, getting to markets. Outside debts, or how long the cash will last, if there are any. And the few skills that could stop everything if nobody had them. It’s the boring part, I know. But however good everyone is at dealing with each other emotionally, a group can still die because the well fails, or because one exhausted person is the only one who knows where everything is and how it works.

Please Choose the Values Before Falling in Love With the View

People often pick a community the way they’d pick a vacation rental: the land is gorgeous, the sunset shows up in the pond, and everybody seemed really nice when you visited. The pond wins you over on the first date, and then two years later the vaccination policy shows up, with paperwork.
S13v6-2P1P2:
People often pick a community the way they’d pick a vacation rental: the land is gorgeous, the sunset shows up in the pond, and everybody seemed really nice when you visited. The pond wins you over on the first date, and then two years later the vaccination policy shows up, with paperwork.

When you go to visit a community, have a list ready of what you really believe about children, money, property ownership, romance, medicine, food, spiritual practice, technology, privacy, conflict and leaving. Where are you still unsure? Mark those places too.
S13v6-2P3: Add sexuality and gender to the list. Yes, it keeps getting longer. Could an LGBTQ+ member live openly, have relationships and stay fully protected by the community? Should children be taught to question their sexual identities at an early age? What will the community do if one of its kids grows up gay or trans? If a group hasn’t answered these yet, it hasn’t finished working out its values on freedom or on raising children, either. Your list should also say whether you’re willing to experiment. That’s a real value too, and it has to be declared, because the person next to you may think the experimenting ended in 1978 and whatever came out of it is doctrine now.
S13v6-2P4: Then compare your values with the group’s real behavior, as well as with its public language. Ask how they handled a recent conflict, who can block a decision, what happened to the last person who left, and who owns the land. Those are uncomfortable conversations, but the view will still be there afterward.
S13v6-4P1: When The Farm grew fast, a lot of the people who came were in need, and there weren’t many filters that worked. Being open to everybody felt so spiritual! The practical burden piled up anyway. A membership process is there to protect both the people who are already there and the newcomers. It’s no good for anyone to join a group that can’t deliver what it promised.
